He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] and the [[California Baptist Lancers men's basketball|California Baptist Lancers]]. ==Early life== Acquaah was raised in [[Bakersfield, California]] and attended Warren Middle School.{{cite news |last1=Cunningham |first1=Clay |title=CSUB looks to contain Bakersfield native Acquaah, Lancers |url=https://www.bakersfield.com/sports/college/csub-looks-to-contain-bakersfield-native-acquaah-lancers/article_9ab993ec-3186-11ea-b943-cb2746bb71f6.html |accessdate=March 17, 2020 |work=[[The Bakersfield Californian]] |date=January 7, 2020}} He began his high school career at [[Chino Hills High School]] and befriended [[Lonzo Ball]] after meeting him at a gym in [[Los Angeles]]. Acquaah is mentioned on Ball's hip hop album ''Born 2 Ball''. Acquaah transferred to [[La Salle College Preparatory|La Salle College Prep]].{{cite news |last1=Lawson |first1=Theo |title=Milan Acquaah announces transfer from Washington State, becomes fourth guard to leave program |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/apr/27/milan-acquaah-announces-transfer-from-washington-s/ |accessdate=March 17, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=April 27, 2018}} He transferred again to [[Cathedral High School (Los Angeles)|Cathedral High School]] and played alongside [[Kobe Paras]]. Acquaah made a game-winning three-pointer to win the San Fernando Valley Invitational championship in December 2014.{{cite news |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=Boys' basketball: Cathedral wins championship on Milan Acquaah's three |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-cathedral-wins-championship-on-milan-acquaahs-three-at-the-buzzer-20141223-story.html |accessdate=March 17, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 23, 2014}} Acquaah was regarded as a three-star prospect, the No. 39 point guard in his class, and signed with Washington State in November 2015.{{cite web |last1=Nusser |first1=Jeff |title=Milan Acquaah, Jeff Pollard sign letters of intent with Washington State |url=https://www.cougcenter.com/2015/11/11/9715250/milan-acquaah-jeff-pollard-sign-wsu-basketball-recruiting |website=Coug Center |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=March 17, 2020 |date=November 11, 2015}} ==College career== Acquaah began his collegiate career at [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] where he redshirted his freshman season. During his redshirt year, coach [[Ernie Kent]] called him "unguardable" during scrimmages. As a redshirt freshman, Acquaah averaged 4.9 points and 1.9 assists per game, making nine starts. He scored a season-high 13 points during a loss to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. After the season, Acquaah announced he was transferring. Acquaah opted to move to [[California Baptist Lancers men's basketball|California Baptist]], which was transferring to Division I, and was granted a waiver for immediate eligibility. He scored 36 points in a win against [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] on January 3, 2019.{{cite web |last1=Mitchell |first1=Greg |title=A year later, Milan Acquaah is having the star turn he envisioned |url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2019/1/14/18177479/a-year-later-milan-acquaah-is-having-the-star-turn-he-envisioned |website=Mid-Major Madness |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=March 17, 2020 |date=January 14, 2019}} As a redshirt sophomore, Acquaah averaged 19.0 points and 5.0 rebounds per game. He was named [[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] player of the week honors twice and was named WAC Newcomer of the Year and First Team All-Conference.{{cite news|title=2019 WAC Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|url=https://wacsports.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20190311p9oozv|accessdate=March 12, 2019|work=[[Western Athletic Conference]]|date=March 12, 2019|archive-date=May 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190511141147/https://www.wacsports.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20190311p9oozv|url-status=dead}} After the season, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but decided to return to California Baptist.{{cite news |last1=Alexander |first1=Jim |title=Alexander: NBA draft process was an education for CBU's Milan Acquaah |url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2019/10/17/alexander-nba-draft-process-was-an-education-for-cbus-milan-acquaah/ |access-date=March 17, 2020 |work=[[The Press-Enterprise]] |date=October 17, 2019}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=205 players filed as early-entry candidates for the 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/04/28/205-players-early-entry-candidates-2020-nba-draft-deadline/ |accessdate=April 30, 2020 |work=Rookie Wire |date=April 28, 2020}} ==Professional career== On July 25, 2021, Acquaah signed his first professional contract with [[Enosis Neon Paralimni B.C.|Enosis Neon Paralimni]] of the [[Cyprus Basketball Division A]].{{cite web |title=E.N. Paralimni tabs rookie Milan Acquaah |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com//news/EN-Paralimni-tabs-rookie-Milan-Acquaah/696125 |website=[[Eurobasket.com]] |access-date=July 29, 2021 |date=July 25, 2021}} In November 2021, he received a Hoops Agent Player of the Week award for round 6. He had 34 points, 7 rebounds, and 8 assists.{{cite web |title=Milan Acquaah claims Cypriot OPAP Basket League weekly honour |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Cyprus/news/714855/Milan-Acquaah-claims-Cypriot-OPAP-Basket-League-weekly-honour |website=eurobasket.com |access-date=March 4, 2025}} In January 2023, Acquaah signed with [[Apollon Limassol B.C.]]{{cite web |title=Milan Acquaah is a newcomer at Apollon |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Cyprus/news/787126/Milan-Acquaah-is-a-newcomer-at-Apollon |website=eurobasket.com |access-date=January 10, 2025}} On June 24, 2024, Acquaah signed with [[BK Inter Bratislava]]. He had previously been the top scorer at Apollon where he averaged 17.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Inter Bratislava sign a second import player |url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Ghana/news/877965/Inter-Bratislava-sign-a-second-import-player |website=afrobasket.com |access-date=January 10, 2025}} ==Personal life== Acquaah is the son of Tracy Acquaah and Michelle Johnson. He is an only child.{{cite web |title=Milan Acquaah - Men's Basketball |url=https://cbulancers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/milan-acquaah/6527 |website=CBU Athletics |access-date=March 4, 2025
